messages:
harry: POC with NovaRetail. They're shipping logs+traces from Windows Fluentd -> our hosted ingest and seeing sporadic 429s. Also traces not appearing in Console when they search the trace id. Can we triage? cc @tess @diego :wave:

tess: Do we have a sample Fluentd config and a raw request they send? 429s usually correlate with batched payload size or token throughput on the key.

harry: They pasted this minimal example and a curl replicate: 

fluent snippet:
<match app.logs>
  @type http
  endpoint https://api.redwood.ai/v1/logs
  serializer json
  <buffer>
    @type memory
    chunk_limit_size 2m
    flush_interval 10s
  </buffer>
</match>

payload (trimmed): {"events":[{"msg":"checkout","trace_id":"trace-9"},{"msg":"charge","trace_id":"trace-9"}]}

curl -> response 429 + Retry-After: 8

diego: Quick fixes: 1) reduce chunk_limit_size to ~256k or set batch_size=20 so requests are small 2) implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After 3) inject X-Request-Id or traceparent header so Console can index the trace id.

tess: Example header mapping for out_http: <request_headers> X-Request-Id: ${record["trace_id"]} </request_headers> — confirm plugin version supports interpolation.

infra-bot: Note: I logged an internal ticket to check if the customer's API key hit a soft throughput cap. ticket #INFR-8421.

observability-bot: Quick link: Console traces?q=x-request-id:trace-9 -> https://console.redwood.ai/traces?q=x-request-id:trace-9

harry: We handed them a short checklist: lower chunk, add header mapping or proxy to inject header, enable retry/backoff. Also asked sales to request a temporary higher-limit key for testing.

tess: If header injection doesn't show traces, have them capture a raw request (tcpdump or curl copy) and paste it here so we can confirm header presence.

harry: Will follow up after they test. Thanks everyone :pray:
